## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`test_rejects_legacy_header` needs fixing because it can't fail if the header version check regresses. The header change in `parse_report` itself is correct, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` does exercise it.

## Changes
`parse_report` now accepts only the exact header `REPORT v1`; before this change, any line starting with `REPORT ` was accepted. Two tests are added that are meant to check that unsupported headers are rejected.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:11 — tests — Make the legacy-header test build a complete v0 report — Your `rsplit` call turns `"REPORT v1\nversion=v1"` into `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`, which leaves the header as `v1` and has no `END` line. `parse_report` therefore returns `None` at `app/report.py:3`, before the header check runs. The comment at line 9 says the version is changed to v0, but only the body line changes. — The test passes even with the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check, so it gives no protection against regressions in the version check it claims to guard. — Fix: Use a fixture like `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or delete this test because `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that case.
